brief: RBC BlueBay's Mark Dowding argues a tech stock retreat drove Treasury yields lower as investors sought safety, and flags OpenAI's recent stumble as a possible sign the AI-driven earnings-momentum trajectory is starting to level off. If that continues over coming weeks, it could trigger a larger stock reversal, which would make core rates markets more attractive. He cites a private portfolio company whose underlying firms are flattening AI spend after exponential growth, and says rate-squeezed non-AI companies and CEOs more broadly are shifting toward cost containment, with token spend now being rationed after an initial free-for-all. He stresses the AI buildout itself is not stopping, just moderating, which would still support a healthy, if less accelerating, 2027 U.S. growth outlook. On rates, DC meetings cemented his view that the next Fed hike comes no earlier than December, with hikes expected in Q4 and Q1 2027 before inflation, seen peaking near 4%, declines and the Fed holds. He stays constructive at the front end but cautious on longer bonds given rising term premia from debt growth, favoring a steepening curve. Energy prices are flagged as a wildcard, with a Middle East de-escalation deal seen as unlikely.
